steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease two baking sheets.
Sift flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together in a bowl.

Cream butter, white sugar, and brown sugar in a large bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy. Beat in one egg at a time, then stir in vanilla. Gradually stir in flour mixture. Fold in oats and chocolate chips. Drop by rounded teaspoonfuls onto the prepared baking sheets.
Bake in batches in the preheated oven until set, 8 to 10 minutes. Allow cookies to cool on baking sheets for 5 minutes before removing to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Cowboy Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These cowboy cookies are loaded with chocolate chips and oats! Look the other way if you're a fan of crunchy cookies as these are soft and chewy.
raw_recipe.name: Cowboy Cookies

review.reviewBody: Okay, here's what I did to combat the "flat" problem: used 3/4Cup of both sugars instead of a full cup, used 1 egg plus one yolk, increased vanilla to 2 teaspoons (just cause I like them flavorful) increased temp to 375 for 8-9 mins. and wha lah! PERFECTION! DELICIOUS cookies will make again. Thanks for a great recipe!

I have been making this cookie recipe for 35 years with the only difference being we use a whole bag 12oz. of semisweet chocolate chips. My mom made them for 20 years before me. They are the best chocolate chip cookies you will find. Why people change the recipe is beyond me! They are not even the same cookie if you change them...so why? Anyway, they are delicious and I don't know one person who does not love them in all my years of baking them.

I halved the recipe and used 1/3c of each sugar. I then added 1/4 c of each chocolate chips, white chocolate chips, PB chips, shredded coconut, and pecans. I also toasted the oats for a few min on a frying pan. My cookies are always flat but these ones were nice and fluffy. I did sift the flour mixture.

I made these as written subbing cup 4 cup gluten free flour for all purpose. In addition, I had to go run a couple surprise errands so ended up chilling the cookie dough after making it for maybe 4 hours. As written this recipe created a sticky cookie dough that spread when it baked. In addition it needed extra baking time. The resulting cookie was sweet and chewy, it wasn't a bad cookie or the best cookie ever, somewhere in the middle. For my family of cookie monsters they were not good enough to devour all of while I was at practice (I made a half batch). Tweaking the recipe as many others have done may move this cookie to that best cookie ever position. Tweaks that maybe beneficial could include adjusting the amount of sugar (reducing it), adding more flour, using a shortening/butter mix, chilling the dough longer to adjusting the baking temp.

The trick: cold dough & cold cookie sheets.
Put dough & cookie sheets in freezer for 15 - 20 min. (Air bake cookie sheets are the best) 
Bake one batch at a time, alternating the cold cookie sheets & keeping dough in freezer. 
The cold dough doesn't melt into a flat blob when you put it in the oven. The cookies are moist & chewy & fat. . Also, add walnuts.

I made this recipe exactly as written and ended up with flat greasy cookies. I added about 1/4 cup of flour and bumped the temperature to 375. Also, i refridgerator the dough.... all of which fixed that issue. Then I decided I wanted a but more cruch, so added a cup if chopped walnuts and a cup of unsweetened shredded coconut. With all of these modifications , these were some of the best cookies I've ever made. But... can't give 5 stars, because when it all came down to it... I didn't really follow the recipe, but my own instincts.

This recipe also makes a FANTASTIC COOKIE BAR! I have no cookie sheet and was craving an oatmeal chocolate chip cookie. I put the whole recipe into a greased 13 by 9 inch pan and they came out GREAT! I also was out of vanilla and low on sugar so I put in a quarter cup less sugar. I had no brown sugar, so I substituted white and added a teaspoon of mollassas to it. They still came out DELISH!! Next time, I'm gonna follow the whole recipe and use nuts as well! THANKS FOR SHARING THE GREAT RECIPE!!

These are my husbands favorite cookies. I use 3/4 cup of each sugar and 1/2 Cup butter 1/2 Cup shortening + 1Tblsp water. & 2tsp of vanilla. I added coconut and used 2 kinds of chocolate, milk and semi-sweet and chopped pecans. I set my oven to 375 although I suspect it is a bit cooler than that, more like 365 so I had to cook them for 15 minutes. I used a small scoop that is approximately a full Tblsp. The cookies came out perfectly. Not flat at all. I had lost my recipe for these so was very happy to find this one. Thanks for posting it!
I make mine with the addition of some shredded coconut and I use 1/4 cup measuring cup for putting out the dough.
3/4 cups of each sugar; double the choc chips; add chia seeds; two egg whites + one yolk so not too crunchy

I, too, decreased the sugars and increased the vanilla. But, I also added one more trick. I warmed the butter to melting before adding the brown sugar so some of the crystals actually dissolved. I also added 2 T of milk for longevity and chewiness. My family loved them. All my friends say I need more practice -- but they say that just so they can get more of these yummy yummy in your tummy cookies. My diet is shot to heck!
My husband told me that it is the best cookie that I have ever made.

This is almost exactly like my grandma’s recipe for cowboy cookies. She always added some chopped walnuts. I don’t have a measurement because we’re from the South and we go by “until it looks right” as a unit of measurement, lol! But it’s absolutely delicious with or without nuts!

So made these cookies and they turned out amazing. But what they are is basically an oatmeal chocolate chip cookie. They are not a true cowboy cookie. But that's okay cuz now I am making another recipe that our cowboy cookies. So my household is going to have a lot of cookies here LOL

I always read the others comments. I did replace 1/2 of the oats with unsweetened coconut, I cut back on the sugar, added both raisin and chocolate chips in equal quantities, no added nuts. I always chill my dough overnight before baking. My cookies were not flat at all. My baking time was 11 minutes in an electric oven and I am at sea level. I needed a new cookie for my rotation and these do the trick. Thank you.
Followed the recipe exactly and while the cookies taste ok, they are way too sweet, spread too thin when baking and don’t hold together well. Probably would not use this recipe again.
This is a fantastic recipe and was loved by our group of dinner friends.
This was a great recipe. Yummmy!
Everyone really liked the flavor and texture of these cookies. They were also easy to make which was very nice.
